Description:

Name: AutoFAB
Description:
AutoFAB is building the world's first autonomous fabrication cell, a desktop factory that designs, prints, and assembles hardware end-to-end, without a human in the loop.

We started with a simple observation: the bottleneck in hardware development isn't ideas. It's the brutal, repetitive loop of fabricating, assembling, and iterating physical prototypes. Hardware startups burn months and tens of thousands of dollars just getting parts in hand. We're building AutoFAB to collapse that loop to hours.

The AutoFAB cell combines a 3D printer with robot arms, and a physical AI stack into a single unified system. It learns from human demonstrations via teleoperation, then runs autonomously. Every cycle makes it faster, more accurate, and more capable. This is Wright's Law applied to robotic fabrication: the more it builds, the better it gets, and the cheaper it becomes to build the next thing.

Our customers are robotics & hardware startups, teams that need physical prototypes fast and can't afford to be blocked by fabrication. 

But AutoFAB isn't just a tool for startups. It's infrastructure.

The long-term thesis: self-replicating factories. Systems that can reproduce and expand their own production capacity without human labor at every step. SpaceX is building the transport layer to make humanity multi-planetary. AutoFAB is building the production layer, the factories that will follow. Every asteroid, every lunar base, every orbital station will need the ability to fabricate on-site. That requires autonomous, self-replicating manufacturing at the frontier.

If you're a hardware founder blocked by fabrication, an investor who believes in physical AI, or a builder who wants to work on something that matters at civilizational scale, we want to talk.

The factory builds itself. Let's get to work.

The result is a costly “tune, fly, crash, rebuild” cycle where each failure can mean weeks of physical rework.

Aerial Avionics focuses on a reliability-first controller layer, with disciplined test infrastructure and repeatable demo flights that prove unattended performance. As BVLOS rules relax and autonomous fleets scale, the reliability bar is rising. Aerial Avionics is building the controller foundation commercial autonomy demands.

Forge is currently focused on contract manufacturing for aerospace and hardware startups, supporting teams that require high-precision production but face scaling constraints. In parallel, we are investing heavily in R&D around laser welding, a key enabling technology for automated, high-performance manufacturing.

Laser welding is a natural starting point because welding is often the bottleneck in production lines, manual processes like TIG are significantly slower than upstream automated steps, such as cutting or stamping. Laser welding addresses this directly: it is typically 2–10× faster, produces minimal distortion due to a small heat-affected zone, and requires little to no post-processing. This makes it highly compatible with automation and ideal for consistent, high-throughput production.

This work will culminate in the first Forge Module: a laser welding unit designed as a foundational building block for modular, scalable factories that overcome labour shortages rather than replacing jobs.

Using advanced methods — including model-based control, deep imitation and reinforcement learning, domain randomization, and model-in-the-loop / hardware-in-the-loop testing — we train and tune control and perception stacks until they transfer robustly to real devices.

That simulation-first approach enables three parallel product tracks:
	•	Consumer home robots that reliably handle the top 10 repetitive tasks (lighting, laundry, dishwashing, vacuuming, folding, etc.).
	•	A speed-performance robot platform engineered for agility and low-latency control in high-tempo applications.
	•	Industrial robotic systems and integrations designed for throughput, repeatability and safe collaboration on factory floors.

Why this matters: simulation + disciplined tuning reduces field failures, shortens development cycles, and makes safe, predictable automation practical at scale. We pair that with full product engineering — sensors, embedded compute, mechanical design, and in-house manufacturing — so our models don’t just perform in the lab, they perform at home and on the line.

Core pillars:
	•	Digital twins & physics-accurate simulation for safe, repeatable training.
	•	Sim-to-real transfer techniques (domain randomization, calibrations, HIL).
	•	Advanced learning: deep RL, imitation learning, and model-based controllers.
	•	End-to-end product engineering and manufacturing for consumer and industrial robots.
	•	Safety, privacy and compliance as fundamental design constraints.

Today, manipulation models are stuck on a hard problem: most robot-training data is vision-only. But contact, force, and slip are exactly what hands rely on — and what cameras can't see. Without touch, a model can recognize a part but still can't reliably grasp, insert, or handle it. That's the data bottleneck holding back real-world manipulation.

We close that gap. 6thSense captures synchronized vision and touch — tactile-paired training data — from real human settings wearing low-cost tactile gloves and an egocentric camera. Everyday manual work becomes high-fidelity, tactile-paired demonstrations for training and evaluating manipulation models.

6thSense is backed by Y Combinator (S26), and our data is collected on real human settings — not in a lab. If you're building manipulation models or robots talk to us.

Name: HOPR Capstone 2025-26
Description: The Hopping Observation Platform for Reconnaissance (HOPR) is a lunar jumping robot developed to investigate permanently shadowed regions and collect imagery of potential ice deposits near the Moon’s poles. Lunar ice represents a vital in-situ resource for future missions, offering potential sources of water, oxygen, and propellant. HOPR’s primary objective is to capture high-resolution images and terrain data to support future exploration and resource utilization HOPR utilizes a compact, spring-powered hopping mechanism that enables mobility across uneven terrain in low gravity. Its lightweight structure, efficient power system, and elastic energy storage system allow it to operate effectively within hazardous environments traditional rovers cannot reach. By combining a jumping mobility approach with an on-board data collection system, HOPR demonstrates a practical approach to reconnaissance in extreme conditions. The platform serves as a proof of concept for small, agile robotic explorers capable of enhancing lunar surface studies and supporting the development of sustainable exploration infrastructure.

Team Techno was founded with the sole intent of progressing within the field of robotics and becoming familiar with the new wave of automation that was accompanying the 4th Industrial Revolution. Its founders, a group of undergraduate students from Ghulam Ishaq Khan Institute of Engineering Sciences and Technology (GIKI), were a passionate bunch whose determination finally paid off when the team came into being in 2015.

The team had a humble beginning with only a handful of student body forming the student body. Today the team boasts a network of 30+ alumni spread across different continents along with more than 35+ active members engaged within the different modules and domains of the team.

Description:
CoreFrame Labs is an early-stage technology company focused on developing artificial intelligence and robotics systems designed to automate complex real-world tasks.

The company’s work centers around computer vision, intelligent sensing, and robotic systems capable of operating in environments where automation has historically been difficult to deploy. By combining AI-driven perception with practical robotics engineering, CoreFrame Labs aims to develop technologies that improve efficiency, reduce labor dependency, and enable new capabilities across multiple industries.

One of the company’s current research initiatives focuses on AI-powered fruit detection and harvesting systems designed for specialty crop agriculture, where labor shortages and rising costs have created significant demand for automation solutions.

CoreFrame Labs is actively exploring applications of AI vision and robotics across agriculture, industrial automation, and emerging robotic platforms.

At Turul Robotics, we deliver complete solutions that combine robotic flexibility with CNC precision. We help manufacturers achieve the next level of automation through multi-axis robotic machining, hybrid manufacturing, friction stir welding, and a myriad of other processes — all powered by Siemens NX CAM Robotics and Siemens SINUMERIK controls.

Our expertise lies in the most complex CNC robotic applications, including 6 to 8-axis robotic milling, additive + subtractive hybrid manufacturing, and CAM to Controller digital twin simulation. Each system we design is optimized in NX to ensure collision-free motion, toolpath accuracy, and perfect synchronization between robots and controller.

As authorized partners and resellers of Siemens Digital Industries Software, Siemens SINUMERIK hardware, and robotic systems from KUKA, Comau, and MABI, we provide complete, turnkey solutions — from simulation and design to installation, commissioning, and training.

Our approach bridges the gap between industrial robotics and CNC machining, empowering manufacturers in aerospace, marine, energy, automotive, and advanced composites to produce parts faster, more flexibly, and with uncompromising precision.

The name Turul is a nod to our founder’s roots — the mythical bird of the old Hungarian tribes, symbolizing vision, strength, and innovation. Like the Turul guiding explorers toward new horizons, Turul Robotics guides customers into the future of intelligent manufacturing.

Mission:
To make complex robotic manufacturing simple, powerful, and accessible — enabling manufacturers of all sizes to innovate with precision, flexibility, and confidence.

Description:
EvoLogics GmbH is a German-based high-tech enterprise. The company was founded in 2000 by a group of leading international scientists and R&D experts aimed to develop innovative key technologies for maritime and offshore industries through interdisciplinary cooperation between engineering and life sciences.

EvoLogics GmbH designs and manufactures underwater information and communication systems based on bionic concepts, combining cutting edge engineering with the best ideas found in nature. The advanced product features have become enabling technologies for deep water exploration and production. 

EvoLogics’ products offer highly reliable, flexible and cost-effective solutions for multiple underwater communication, positioning, navigation and monitoring applications. The team strives for innovation and invests its vast experience into developing, manufacturing and supporting  products that deliver an excellent performance and solve the most challenging tasks.

EvoLogics' developments are based on the patented S2C (Sweep Spread Carrier) technology - the most reliable acoustic telemetry available for subsea and offshore applications that provides an independent bidirectional data link along with acoustic positioning, broadcasting and full networking capabilities. The company’s solutions can simultaneously facilitate optimal operation and navigation of subsea robots. They enable retrieving information from various subsea sensors and other subsystems and allow to control complex processes by combining communication with high-accuracy positioning and multiple monitoring options.

S2C systems have been carefully designed for operations in harsh underwater environments and enhanced with special algorithms for signal processing and data management. The company’s extensive experience with sensor integration allows it to provide customers with turn-key solutions ranging from initial deployment up to recovering the equipment.

Name: Remedy Robotics
Description:
Remedy Robotics exists to bring flawless, immediate, endovascular intervention (EI)—treatment for stroke, heart attack, bleeding, aneurysmal disease, pulmonary embolism and more— to every patient worldwide. Remedy is the only company in the world to have performed:
- Completely robotic neurointerventional procedures in humans from start to finish.
- Completely remote robotic neurointerventional procedures in humans from from start to finish.
- Autonomous endovascular navigation.

A few key principles underlie our work. We strongly believe that:
- EI is optimizable. Tool movements should be deliberate and efficient. Procedures should be fast and effective. Complications should be avoided without exception.
- All patients at elite US institutions deserve access to flawless EI without delay. But so do all patients at smaller US community hospitals. And so do all patients in Kinshasa and Port Moresby and Alice Springs and anywhere in the world.
- The world's finest technology and technologists should focus on advancing our health and wellbeing. They belong at Remedy Robotics.

Misty Robotics is introducing a new way of entering the world of robotics. With Misty, a friendly and highly sophisticated educational robot platform, we are opening up access to robots in STEM education and research by taking down today’s barriers - cost, required knowledge of robotics and the efforts needed for different groups in society to explore and learn about robots. 

The Misty robot provides researchers, innovators and educators with an easy-to-use and creative tool to explore social robotics, ranging from quick and simplistic prototypes to advanced human-robot interactions. By leveraging the power of the social robotics community, Misty users can share their experiences and quickly gain traction in their development and research.

Misty Robotics are creating new opportunities for the research and innovation industry to further understand how social robots will be useful in our society. Misty Robotics believes in the role and positive impact that robots will have in our lives, and is part of the early revolution together with researchers and innovators to define the future role of robots in society.

Name: MVP Robotics, Inc.
Description:
MVP Robotics began as a collaboration between Dartmouth head football coach Buddy Teevens and a group of engineers and athletes from Dartmouth's Thayer School of Engineering and together they developed the world’s first robotic tackling dummy to help reduce unnecessary contacts and the incidence of injuries suffered during football and other sporting practices.  In the first 2 years of the robotic tackling dummies (MVP|DRIVES) being available, MVP completely sold out of their MVP|DRIVES to half the NFL, 40+ colleges, and more than 75 high schools.  At Dartmouth, concussions were reduced by 58% in the first two seasons of implementing the MVP|DRIVES into practice.  The MVP|DRIVES are designed to accurately simulate the size and performance of a human, weighing 190 lbs and reaching speeds of 17 mph.

Following the successful development and introduction of the world’s first robotic tackling dummy (MVP|DRIVE) for football, MVP has continued developing their patented robotic system to create HEKTR (Humanoid Engageable Kinetic Training Robot) in order to fit the realistic tactical training needs of the warfighter.  HEKTR is a remote-control, fully armored, all-terrain, and responsive live-fire target that simulates a realistic environment by reaching speeds over 20 mph and providing instantaneous feedback to the shooter.  The HEKTR platform is a versatile training tool that forces quick reaction and fluid decision making from operators in any setting, including: house, urban, woodland, desert, ice/snow, and sand.  Through the HEKTR mobile app, operators are able to control and customize their training scenarios and thereby integrate HEKTR’s capabilities as part of larger training evolutions.

Name: Glidance
Description:
For over 300 million people worldwide who are blind or have low vision, independent navigation remains the single greatest barrier to freedom and personal agency.  

Glidance exists to change that — and in doing so, lay the foundation for how intelligent machines will one day move among us: safely, and in ways that extend human capability rather than replace it. 

Founded by Amos Miller — a blind technologist who pioneered spatial augmented reality at Microsoft Research and led Microsoft Soundscape — Glidance is an autonomous technology company building the future of robotics and intelligent wayfinding to serve real human needs.  

Breakthroughs in AI, computer vision, and robotics over the past few years have opened new frontiers in understanding the physical world — and with it, the ability to help people move through it. 

Glide is the first meaningful evolution in primary mobility aids for the blind and low vision community in nearly a century. Affordable, easy to use, and quick to learn, it physically guides you through both familiar and new environments. It uses real-time data from an array of advanced sensors to map the best routes, identify targets of interest, and avoid obstacles to get you safely to your destination. 

It is the product of years of work by our team of engineers, researchers, designers, O&M specialists, and AI and machine learning specialists, developed alongside a community of more than 8,000 blind and low vision individuals and leading academic institutions. Our philosophy is that every decision should come from rigorous testing and feedback by those whose lives will be most impacted by it. 

We look forward to having you with us on this journey.

Description:
Fabrica AI invented an autonomous tile grouting robot that operates with a single press of a button powered by Computer Vision and Robot Operating System (ROS). The robot is able to fill up the grout in all the grout lines and navigate past obstacles such as pipes and drain holes to automate the tile grouting process. Human intervention is only needed to move the robot from room to room, reload grout, and change water, and the robot does not need to be supervised while in operation. Real-time mapping of the rooms (including irregularly shaped corridors and the main living area) and grout an entire apartment with no need to upload any floor plan beforehand. No BIM or any prior set-up is required. The robot is small (under 60cm on each side),  reasonably lightweight (roughly 60kg), and can be easily operated by one person and able to navigate tight spaces such as corridors in smaller homes.  
Besides, using the robot means that workers do not need to bend down for grouting which may hurt their knees and back over time. Our robot also ensures high quality of grouting as it is consistently able to compress grout within gaps and not just produce a nice surface finish. This will prevent grout from falling out over time leaving behind hollow gaps in tile joints where dirt can accumulate.

Name: Partenit | Reasoning & Safety Layer for Robots
Description:
Partenit — Reasoning & Safety Layer for Robots

Partenit is a deterministic decision-making layer for robots operating in real-world, safety-critical environments.
We sit between high-level task planning and low-level execution, validating every robot action before it happens.

Modern robots increasingly rely on LLM-based planners, but pure LLMs hallucinate, break safety constraints, and cannot be audited. Classical rule-based systems are safe but brittle and slow to adapt. Partenit combines the strengths of both.

Our approach uses a Propose → Validate architecture:
LLMs generate candidate actions, while Partenit enforces hard safety rules, operational policies, and physical constraints using ontologies and deterministic validation. Unsafe or non-compliant actions are blocked by design and replaced with safe alternatives — with a full explanation of why.

Partenit provides:
- Deterministic, hallucination-free robot decisions
- Explainable reasoning traces suitable for audits and incident analysis
- Rule-based guarantees for safety, compliance, and operations
- Hardware-agnostic integration with existing robot stacks (ROS / skills)

We do not replace perception, control, or motion planning.
We provide the missing layer that decides what a robot is allowed to do, when, and why.

Partenit is designed for warehouses and other regulated environments where robots must operate reliably among people, follow strict procedures, and handle unexpected situations without unsafe behavior.

Our mission is simple:
make AI-powered robots deployable in production, not just impressive in demos.

We transform robots into trusted teammates who can think, communicate, and work naturally alongside humans. Our breakthrough technology combines advanced cognitive reasoning with precise robotic control, enabling robots to:

Understand and explain their decisions in natural language
Learn new skills through demonstration and conversation
Work as true team members
Adapt intelligently to new situations and challenges

Whether for maintenance, logistics, or collaborative tasks, HARMONIC-powered robots bring human-like intelligence to robotic systems while maintaining industrial-grade reliability and safety. We're making human-robot teaming more natural, effective, and trustworthy.

Building the future of human-robot collaboration, one teammate at a time.

Name: PACE Robotics
Description: Startup automation company that offers robotic programming, off-line programming, troubleshooting, consulting and integration services for Fanuc, Kuka, and ABB systems in a variety of application, welding, sealing, urethane, and material handling.

Name: Hank robotics LLC
Description:
At Hank Robotics, we believe no one should risk their life to keep a building clean. Traditional façade cleaning with ropes and scaffolds is dangerous, costly, and disruptive. We’re changing that.

Using FAA-certified drone technology, we deliver:
High-rise window & façade cleaning
Garage, sidewalk & flat surface cleaning
Solar, wind turbine & water tower maintenance
Aerial inspections & compliance-ready reports

Our mission is simple: protect lives, cut costs, and redefine how the world maintains buildings.
Forward-thinking property managers partner with Hank Robotics to:
Eliminate safety risks
Reduce operating costs
Get data-driven reporting
Clean 2x faster than old methods

We’re not just cleaning buildings. We’re building the future of building maintenance.

Name: IEEE Purdue University Fort Wayne
Description: The IEEE Purdue Fort Wayne (PFW) Student Chapter stands as a committed extension of the global IEEE community, uniquely positioned within one of Indiana’s most technically inclined academic institutions. It exists not as a formality or a résumé filler, but as a deliberate space for students to engage in meaningful, applied, and future-oriented activities in electrical engineering, computer science, and allied technical disciplines. The chapter functions with clarity: to advance technical competence, professional growth, and community impact. Every event, initiative, and strategy traces back to this core.

Name: Mefferdi
Description:
Welcome to Mefferdi – a pioneering underwater ocean robotics company dedicated to exploring the unknown and unlocking the full potential of the deep blue. We merge cutting-edge robotics, AI-driven systems, and advanced engineering to empower marine research, environmental monitoring, industrial operations, and defense initiatives beneath the waves.

Our state-of-the-art solutions are engineered to thrive in extreme environments, delivering unmatched precision, reliability, and efficiency for both scientific discovery and maritime defense. By integrating robust defense applications into our innovative platforms, we contribute to safeguarding our underwater frontiers and enhancing global maritime security.

Join us on our journey at www.mefferdi.com as we dive into new horizons, make waves in ocean technology, and secure a smarter, safer future below the surface.

Name: UChicago Robotics
Description: UChicago's premier robotics engineering organization.

Name: Overflow Robotics
Description:
A student-led robotics team established in 2020 with a strong record of competitive achievement. The team has won the MATE ROV Regional Championship three consecutive times (2022–2025) and participated in the MATE ROV World Championship twice, achieving 18th place globally in 2024 and 11th in 2025.

The team has also participated in and won multiple robotics competitions across various disciplines. Built and led by dedicated teenagers, it focuses on practical engineering, technical excellence, and the development of real-world robotic systems, with a long-term vision of delivering impactful and innovative solutions within the robotics industry.

Name: Dynamo
Description:
Heavy duty drones for heavy cargo to impossible places and critical moments.

Beginning with the world's largest quadcopter. Move 5 Tons. Anywhere. Anytime.

In development. More to come.

Name: Flapping-Wing Micro-Air-Vehicle (FWMAV)
Description: The Flapping-Wing Micro Air Vehicle (FWMAV) project, led by students at the University of California, Irvine and sponsored by Professor Haithem Taha, is on a mission to replicate the remarkable flight capabilities found in Mother Nature while maintaining the familiar features of conventional drones. We see a wealth of possibilities for the quadflapper technology, not only in the commercial sector but also in governmental and educational domains. Our current objectives are twofold: firstly, to conduct a comprehensive assessment of the advantages and disadvantages of our propulsion system in comparison to traditional alternatives, and secondly, to create a modular, sturdy unit.

Name: 3DBU
Description:
3DBuffalo (3DBU) is on a mission to make robotics as a whole more affordable for everyone while striving to drive innovation through accessibility without compromising quality. We use power of education to empower the next generation of makers, allowing them to transform their visions into robotic solutions.

Join us today, where we empower innovation through simplicity.

Name: Astrobotics at Virginia Tech
Description: We are a design team based out of Joseph F. Ware Advanced Engineering Laboratory at Virginia Tech. We have members from all disciplines of engineering on our team and are apart of the Aerospace and Ocean Engineering department. We compete in the NASA Lunabotics Competition to build a mining robot that can effectively mine icy gravel in harsh conditions.

Name: BYU FROST Lab
Description: The Field Robotic Systems Lab (FROST Lab) at Brigham Young University is focused on enabling the development of robust and reliable field-robotic systems that are able to consistently perceive, navigate, and perform work in complex unstructured real-world environments.

Name: Spiritify.AI
Description: Spiritify.AI is a high-tech AI innovation company based in Boston, Massachusetts, pioneering the research, development and end-to-end delivery of empathy-driven AI companion robots based on our cutting-edge AIoT Cloud Platform that enrich human life experiences across generations through the power of emotionally intelligent AI technology — passionately advanced by our core LACAE values: Love, Appreciation, Compassion, Acceptance, and Empathy.

Name: BYU Mars Rover
Description:
Here at BYU Mars Rover, crafting a competition ready rover gives BYU capstone students hands-on experience, leadership opportunities, and communication skills.

Capstone students lead the charge with faculty guidance. Our dynamic team is composed of software, mechanical, electrical, and science enthusiasts with an engineering background.

Our skills combine to form a rover ready for the University Rover Challenge equipped with a cutting-edge life detection system, advanced 6 degree of freedom SCARA robot arm, and software system enabling autonomous task completion.

Victories from previous competitions only push us to innovate and improve our rover system. Come join our journey to innovation!

Name: Color Robotics
Description:
Color Robotics is building the operating system for autonomous factories.
We help manufacturers manage and optimize their automation and robotics systems through AI-powered software that unifies visibility, monitoring, and diagnostics across production lines.

Our platform brings version control, intelligent monitoring, and AI-driven root cause analysis to PLC-based systems, helping teams reduce downtime and solve problems faster.
Compatible with any robotic system or hardware vendor, Color Robotics gives manufacturers unprecedented control over their automated operations—without requiring deep technical expertise.

Founded by robotics engineers from Honeywell and leading startups, we’re making industrial automation more connected, intelligent, and accessible.

Name: Actash
Description: Actash is a motivated company that excels in robotic automation services. Our aim is to be the best robotic automation provider by focusing on unique approaches to any manufacturing challenge our customers may have.

Name: RoboGrinder at Virginia Tech
Description: RoboGrinder empowers students to tackle complex engineering problems through competitive robotics. We are a co-founding university of the RoboMaster North America community (now ARC Robotics) and remain dedicated to its growth. Each year the team designs, manufactures, and validates a new fleet of robots from scratch, turning classroom theory into hardware that has to survive real competition. Members work with the same tools and processes used in industry, and while most study engineering, students from every major are welcome.

Name: Oprones
Description:
Oprones builds autonomous inspection systems for hazardous, hard-to-access infrastructure. We combine inspection drones with an AI control tower to turn raw data into fast, decision-ready insights.

We’re looking for advisors and early investors to accelerate our pre-seed phase.
Proudly selected by Launch and Ann Arbor SPARK

Name: Capandji
Description:
Bridging AI and the Physical World

AI is transforming industries, but its impact remains limited in the physical world. To bridge this gap, Capandji develops a robotic hand that mimics human dexterity, adaptability, and strength. Unlike traditional rigid designs, the Capandji Hand is flexible, precise, and safe—capable of handling delicate and complex tasks effortlessly.

Powered by innovative actuation systems and advanced manufacturing, our technology enables cost-efficient, human-like robotics for real-world applications.

Name: Agility Robotics
Description: Industrial humanoids hard at work.

Name: Exotec
Description:
Exotec builds elegant goods-to-person warehouse robotic solutions for the world's largest brands. The company combines the best of hardware and software to offer flexible warehouse systems that drive operational efficiency, add resiliency, and improve working conditions for warehouse operators. 30+ industry-leading brands including Carrefour, Decathlon, Gap, and Uniqlo trust Exotec to improve their operations and profitably navigate rapid shifts in business models and customer expectations.

For more information please visit https://www.exotec.com/

Name: Humanoid
Description:
In a world where artificial intelligence opens up new horizons, our faith in its potential unveils a new outlook where, together, humans and machines build a new future filled with knowledge, inspiration, and incredible discoveries.

The development of a functional humanoid robot underpins an era of abundance and well-being where poverty will disappear, and people will be able to choose what they want to do.

We can imagine millions of bipedal robots doing more work than all human labour does today freeing people from the servitude of some repetitive and boring tasks that nobody likes to perform.

We believe that we have enough abundance to take care of everyone who is displaced. Eventually, providing a universal basic income will lead to the true evolution of our civilization.

Labor shortages loom, as the demands on our built environment rise. With the world’s workforce increasingly moving away from undesirable tasks, the manufacturing, construction, and logistics industries critical to our daily lives are left exposed.

By deploying our general-purpose humanoid robots in environments deemed hazardous or monotonous, we envision a future where human well-being is safeguarded while closing the gaps in critical global labour needs.

Name: 1X
Description:
1X is a leader in humanoid robotics, creating humanoid robots for the home as a first step in developing general purpose robots

1X’s mission is to create an abundance of labor through safe, intelligent humanoids that work alongside people.

Name: Posha
Description:
At Posha, we’re revolutionizing how families experience everyday meals. Imagine a private chef in every kitchen, simplifying life with over 1,000 recipes across 10+ cuisines - effortlessly tailored to personal tastes.

Our mission is inspired by the concept of Posha(n)/(पोषण) - nurture and nourishment. We’re dedicated to creating a world where delicious, home-cooked meals bring families together, with minimal effort.

If you’re passionate about innovation, technology, and building products that enhance lives, join us in shaping the future of smart cooking. At Posha, we ensure nothing stands in the way of love and good food.

Name: Ocean Infinity
Description:
Ocean Infinity is a technology-driven company transforming how ocean operations are carried out. We design, build and operate robotic and uncrewed systems to perform complex work at sea - safer, smarter and with less environmental impact. By combining advanced robotics, software and deep operational experience, we prove that a new, more sustainable model for working in the oceans is not just possible, but already happening.  

We’re a business built for people who are curious, pragmatic and comfortable with complexity. We value plain speaking, thoughtful challenge and sound decision-making in uncertain conditions. Our leaders set the direction, but it’s our people - engineers, technologists and operators, who turn ambition into real-world outcomes.

Name: Origin
Description:
Origin is building the World's First General Purpose Construction Robot that automate interior finishing trades like drywall finishing, painting and more on real job sites.

Construction is a $2T+ industry facing labor shortages, rising costs, and stagnant productivity. While manufacturing, logistics, and automotive have embraced automation, construction remains largely manual.

Origin is developing the world’s first general-purpose construction robot — an AI-powered robotic system designed to work alongside human crews and operate power tools across multiple trades.

Our robots are already deployed on live job sites in New York City in partnership with leading General Contractors and Trade Contractors.

We are on a multi-decade mission to build intelligent robotic systems that enable scalable, high-quality, and cost-efficient construction.

you are a contractor exploring construction automation, or an engineer passionate about robotics, AI, controls systems, and real-world autonomy — we’d love to connect. Careers: https://apply.workable.com/origin-10x

Name: FieldAI
Description: FieldAI is building general robot intelligence for the physical world. FieldAI’s technology enables robots to operate safely and reliably in unstructured environments where most of the world’s work happens, without prior maps, GPS, predefined routes, or supporting infrastructure. Its hardware-agnostic approach works across different robot types, allowing customers to deploy the right form factor for the job. FieldAI robots are deployed globally across hundreds of customer sites on three continents, supporting industries including construction, energy, security, and manufacturing. Founded by veterans of NASA JPL, DARPA, and Google DeepMind, FieldAI is bringing AI off the screen and into the field.

Name: Gecko Robotics
Description:
Gecko Robotics is the pioneer of AI + Robotics [AIR technology], transforming how the world builds, operates, and maintains its most critical infrastructure for a more reliable and sustainable future. Using fixed sensors and robots that climb, crawl, swim, and fly, we combine first-order data layers with the predictive power of AI into a single source of truth for the physical world. Cantilever is our operating platform, powered by AIR technology, that empowers teams to achieve operational excellence through actionable data for immediate and long-term planning.

Improve operations. Optimize capital outlay. Extend asset life. That's our promise.

Name: Skild AI (Fetch Robotics)
Description: Fetch Robotics, now part of Skild AI, is the pioneer of On-Demand Automation — the only solution that deploys safe, reliable, and versatile Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMRs) for the warehousing and intralogistics markets in just hours. Together, Fetch Robotics and Zebra provide the broadest range of AMR solutions in the industry resulting in demonstrable improvements in throughput, efficiency and productivity within both commercial and industrial environments — all while working alongside people.

Name: Skylark Labs
Description: Skylark Labs is creating a self-learning brain for machines — intelligence that learns on-device, adapts to the world around it, and thinks collectively with others. Inspired by the human brain, it allows machines to grow smarter with every experience, without the cloud, commands, or retraining. Each system learns directly from what it sees, hears, and feels, turning raw perception into understanding and action. When one machine learns, they all learn — sharing insight without sharing data. Together, they form a living network of intelligence that’s always evolving. With this breakthrough, Skylark Labs is making machines truly autonomous — able to learn, act, and evolve as one

Name: Advanced Navigation
Description:
Advanced Navigation is a global leader in navigation and autonomous systems. By leveraging capabilities in software-enhanced hardware, every solution delivers unrivaled capabilities and exceptional performance across land, air, sea and space applications where GPS is unreliable. 

Made possible with extensive research, testing and vertically integrated manufacturing, the company has progressed into deep technology fields, including robotics, inertial, photonic and quantum sensing, artificial intelligence, underwater acoustics, and GPS antennas and receivers. Customers choose Advanced Navigation for rapid product delivery and unmatched technical field expertise.

Headquartered in Sydney, Australia, with research and production facilities nationwide and offices globally. Advanced Navigation is an Australian manufacturer exporting worldwide. #JoinTheAutonomyRevolution

Name: Chef Robotics
Description:
Chef’s mission is to empower humans by accelerating the advent of intelligent machines in the world.

We believe physical AI (robots that can perceive, reason, and act in the real world) represents the next frontier of AI. While software AI has transformed how we work and communicate, the physical world still runs largely on human labor. That world represents 90% of global GDP, and it’s where AI’s impact will be most profound.

Nowhere is this more evident than in food. In 2023, there were over 1.1 million unfilled jobs in food preparation and service. These labor shortages are forcing food companies to leave millions of dollars in unmet demand on the table each year and driving more of the food supply chain offshore, creating significant risks for US food security.

Chef Robotics is building physical AI for food. Our AI-enabled robots handle the flexible, variable work of food assembly and preparation (work that has historically required human intervention). By deploying robots that learn from real production data across hundreds of ingredients and customers, we’ve built the world’s largest real-world food manipulation dataset and become the market leader in food robotics.

The result: food companies can meet demand, grow production, and keep their supply chains onshore, while their teams focus on the work that humans do best.

Name: Blue Robotics
Description: Blue Robotics makes low-cost, high-performance components for marine robotics to enable the next generation of ocean exploration! Based in Torrance, CA, we are a young and innovative company with a diverse and international customer base.

Name: PickNik Robotics
Description:
PickNik accelerates robotics automation, helping companies simplify, accelerate, and deliver unstructured robotics solutions to optimize operations, foster efficiency, and innovate faster.

MoveIt Pro is PickNik's flagship product, a commercial-grade platform for accelerating the development of unstructured robotic arm applications, reducing engineering time and support costs by up to 75%. The platform for quickly building robotic arm applications, with out-of-the-box reference applications, a powerful runtime engine, and easy user interfaces that enables advanced, customizable robotic solutions for all industries.

Name: Pyka
Description:
Pyka’s goal is to provide society with a new form of safe, clean, and cost-effective transportation enabled by autonomous electric aviation. 

To get there, we’re taking a different approach than most. We're applying our technologies to every industry where autonomous electric aircraft can be useful, starting with the highest value and most dangerous jobs. In doing so, we're building game-changing products manufactured at scale, while perfecting the safety, reliability, and capabilities of our autonomy engine and electric propulsion systems. 

We design, develop and manufacture an ecosystem of technologies including proprietary flight control software, avionics, high power density motors, motor controllers, batteries, and custom carbon-fiber composite airframes.

Today, we supply autonomous electric aircraft for cargo transport and crop protection to real-world customers across four separate continents and have secured industry-first regulatory approvals from the FAA. 

Our cargo aircraft enables remote connectivity, enhances express delivery networks, and ensures fast and reliable shipping of critical supplies to areas in need. Our crop protection aircraft offers agricultural services providers and farmers an autonomous tool to make aerial application safer, more precise, and less harmful to surrounding environments. Both vehicles are highly economical to operate, easy to deploy, and significantly reduce C02 emissions in their respective industries.  

What we work on at Pyka makes people’s lives better now and brings the future of electric aviation one step closer each day.

Name: Bedrock Robotics
Description: Bedrock Robotics brings advanced autonomy to the built world, helping the construction industry build at the pace today's society demands. Our technology upgrades existing heavy equipment, enabling truly autonomous operation with expert level quality and superhuman safety. At a time when we need to build faster than ever—from housing to data centers to factories and energy infrastructure—autonomous construction isn't just an innovation, it's an economic necessity.

Name: Ocean Robotics Planet (formerly ROV Planet)
Description:
The Ocean Robotics Planet Magazine is the most focused publication on Unmanned Underwater Vehicles (ROV, AUV, USV) in the Subsea Construction, Defence, Science, Offshore Oil&Gas, and Offshore Renewable Industries.

www.OceanRoboticsPlanet.com

Name: GrayMatter Robotics
Description:
We’re solving the most difficult surface treatment and finishing challenges high-mix, high-variability manufacturers face with our advanced robotics and physics-informed AI technologies. We are transforming the future of manufacturing with robotics and our proprietary GMR-AITM, designed into smart robotic cells that assist humans in tedious and ergonomically challenging tasks. Our mission is to enhance human productivity and improve the quality of life by letting robots empower people.

Based in Los Angeles, California, GrayMatter Robotics has been voted one of the top 50 Best Places to Work in LA by BuiltIn.  We also won the RBR50 Award in 2022 as one of the top 50 innovators in the robotics market.

Name: Nexxis
Description:
Hi we’re Nexxis,

We’re about so much more than just hiring and selling top quality technical equipment.

Our flexible, solutions-driven approach helps our customers make smarter and more profitable business decisions of their own.  When they choose Nexxis as their technical equipment supplier, they enter into a value-driven partnership which enables them to achieve better outcomes for their business and their own clients too.

At the heart of our operation is the supply of an extensive range of leading-edge inspection, testing and measuring equipment for a variety of applications including offshore oil rigs, subsea installations, engines, machinery, mining operations, infrastructure projects and manufacturing processes.   All these products are available for hire, lease or purchase.

We know from experience that industrial projects are fluid and that requirements change all the time.  We also know that our customers’ circumstances are constantly changing and that they need rapid and practical responses.  That’s where our ‘flexible adaptability’ gives our customers a distinct competitive advantage.

Our whole aim is to reduce project downtime so when you buy, lease or hire any of our technical equipment, you enjoy innovative and flexible contract options, the very best and most advanced equipment on the market, highly skilled and experienced technical support and the benefit of our downtime mitigation guarantee.

As a business we keep up with rapidly evolving technological developments and bring you the most advanced equipment in the world with a continually expanding our range to ensure we have the right equipment to suit your needs.

We’re with you all the way. Comprehensive training on all of our products, either at our Perth offices or on-site, ensure that you maximise the benefit of your investment, plus our team of highly skilled and field-trained technicians are available 24/7 for emergency support.

Name: Engineered Arts
Description:
World leaders in humanoid robots for entertainment, information, education and research.
Engineered Arts Ltd produce a range of humanoids including, Ameca our flagship communication humanoid, Ameca Desktop,  RoboThespian the original robot actor and Mesmer, stunning ultra-realistic robots.

Name: Atomic Machines
Description: Atomic Machines is on Earth to radically advance humanity's command of matter.  Our MC-1 manufacturing technology embodies this mission at the micro-scale, both blowing open the design space ("MEMS 2.0") and doing so in a way that enables extremely rapid iteration and scaling to high-volume manufacturing ("thought to thing time").  Our first device product establishes a new price-performance class highly relevant to the AI data center space.

Name: Nimble
Description:
Nimble is building the autonomous supply chain powered by generalist superhumanoid robots.  

Nimble's intelligent general-purpose supply chain superhumanoid is the first robot in the world capable of performing all core warehouse tasks including storage, retrieval, picking, packing, sorting, kitting and more. Our proprietary robot replaces dozens of complex systems, enabling autonomous warehouses that operate at a fraction of the cost and complexity of today’s leading systems.

Our founding team comes from the AI labs at Stanford and Carnegie Mellon. Our board of directors includes famed robotics and AI icons Marc Raibert (founder of Boston Dynamics), Sebastian Thrun (founder of Google X and Waymo) and Fei-Fei Li (former Chief Scientist of AI at Google, Director of Stanford's AI Lab, creator of ImageNet, and CEO of World Labs).

Name: CynLr
Description: CynLr is a visual object intelligence platform that enables industrial robotic arms to see, understand and manipulate any object in random unstructured environments.

Name: Empire
Description:
Empire + Assembly is building the future of home robotics.

We develop intelligent household robots and AI-powered systems designed to make everyday living easier, safer, and more efficient. Our work brings together robotics, artificial intelligence, mobility, smart sensing, software, and human-centered product design to create practical machines built for real homes and real routines.

Assembly is our home robotics platform, focused on capable household assistance including room preparation, object handling, home patrol, pet monitoring, routine support, smart alerts, and personalized in-home automation.

Our mission is to turn advanced technology into products people can trust, use, and live with every day. We are building robotics that feel reliable, useful, beautifully designed, and ready for the future of modern households.

Follow us for product updates, robotics insights, company news, and career opportunities.

Name: Elistair
Description:
Elistair is the global leading manufacturer of automated tethered drone systems for persistent surveillance and emergency communications. The company's products are deployed by police forces, public safety departments, private security companies and governments on over 70 countries.

Visit our website : www.elistair.com

Name: Liquid Robotics
Description: Liquid Robotics, a wholly owned subsidiary of The Boeing Company, designs and manufactures the Wave Glider, the world’s first wave and solar powered uncrewed ocean robot. Based in Herndon, Virginia, and with an Engineering & Test Facility in Hawai’i, Liquid Robotics works with global partners to address many of the planet’s greatest challenges, by transforming how to assess, monitor, and protect the ocean. Since 2007, Liquid Robotics has conducted 100s of Wave Glider missions around the globe, from the Arctic to Antarctica, for customers in the defense, commercial, and science markets.

Name: Trossen Robotics
Description:
Our drive is a passion for helping innovators innovate.

Trossen Robotics is a leading provider of affordable and versatile robotic platforms designed to accelerate innovation in research and industry. Specializing in advanced robotic arms and AI-driven hardware solutions, Trossen Robotics equips organizations—from global institutions like Google DeepMind and Stanford to innovative startups—with powerful tools for machine learning, data collection, and automation. Committed to fostering collaboration, Trossen Robotics supports customers through customized solutions, comprehensive resources, and international partnerships, empowering users to achieve groundbreaking advancements in robotics and artificial intelligence.

Name: Ambi Robotics
Description: We're empowering people to handle more.

Name: Vimaan
Description:
Vimaan is redefining warehouse inventory operations with AI-powered computer vision.

For years, inventory visibility in warehouses and distribution centers has depended on manual counting, scanning, and verification, a slow, error-prone process that absorbs labor hours and never fully closes the accuracy gap. Vimaan changes that.

We call our category Inventory Intelligence: going beyond basic visibility and tracking to give operations teams the ability to capture, reconcile, and act on inventory data without a manual recount to verify it.

Our platform is built on computer vision, not legacy machine vision or barcode-dependent systems, giving teams a live, reconstructed view of physical inventory rather than just recorded transactions. Our core products, StorTRACK, PalletSCAN, and ParcelSCAN, automate cycle counting, inbound receiving, and outbound shipping on this same foundation, helping teams achieve up to 80% lower labor costs and move toward 100% inventory accuracy.

Vimaan is an Amazon portfolio company, Gartner-recognized and already live in some of the world's largest warehouses and distribution centers.

Learn more at vimaan.ai.

Name: Built Robotics
Description: Built Robotics’ mission is to build the robots that build the world. By automating repetitive tasks in the $300 billion solar industry, Built is bridging the workforce gap to accelerate our transition to clean energy.

Name: Matic Robots
Description:
Matic is reimagining the next generation of fully autonomous, helpful, and elegant home robots using AI and computer vision. Level-5 autonomy in your home.

Our flagship product, Matic, is a remarkably smart, proactive, and secure floor-cleaning robot that uses photo-realistic vision with precise 3D mapping to provide a home with perpetually clean floors.

Name: Robust.AI
Description:
Collaborative productivity and Physical AI.

Robust.AI is founded and led by a world-class robotics team. We bring AI, robotics, and human-centered design together to make robots broadly useful, effortless to adopt, and delightful to use. 

CarterTM is novel form of collaborative mobile robot that allows for seamless collaboration with people across picking, putaway and value added service. 

Easy to deploy, Carter integrates with existing systems and requires no infrastructure changes. Real-world adaptability enables our solution to improve throughput, reduce strain on workers, and help retail, e-commerce, and 3PL operations scale smarter and faster.

Name: microagi
Description: microagi, founded in 2025, is a robotics deployment company. Its platform, Atlas, fine-tunes models on a customer’s own operations, drawing on microagi’s proprietary data corpus, and closes the gap between the robot that impresses in a demo and the robot that does reliable work on the line. Atlas is hardware- and model-agnostic: a neutral layerbetween a customer’s infrastructure and frontier AI models, designed to prevent lock-in to any single vendor. microagi is headquartered in Munich, with a research hub in Zurich and offices in London and New York.
Location: New York, New York, United States

Name: Novarc Technologies Inc.
Description:
Novarc activates arc welding robots with perception and cognition. With no visual intelligence these industrial robots currently make costly errors that lead to rework, scrap, rebuilds and downtime. Novarc’s Physical AI  platform combines real-time computer vision, adaptive control, welding intelligence, and over-the-air software deployment to transform robotic welding systems into continuously improving Physical AI endpoints.  Novarc provides a simple pathway to welding intelligence for new cell builds or globally installed arc welding robots.

Novarc’s proprietary technology stack includes innovative weld processes, reliable automation systems, multi-terabyte production welding datasets, AI perception and control systems, and deeply embedded enterprise deployments accumulated over more than a decade

Name: Generalist
Description: Generalist is an AI robotics company building general intelligence for the physical world and making it useful to everyone. The founding team includes engineers from OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Boston Dynamics. The company embraces both large-scale AI and robotics as core to its DNA.

Name: Indy Autonomous Challenge
Description: The IAC organizes fully autonomous racecar competitions among university teams from around the world and works to further automated vehicle technology. The IAC is aiming to establish a hub for performance automation in Indiana by harnessing the power of competition to attract the best and the brightest minds from around the globe.

Name: Fauna Robotics
Description: Robots that live, work, and play by our sides
Location: New York, New York, United States

Name: Mind Robotics
Description:
Mind Robotics is building generalizable robotics for real-world industrial deployment. We believe the fastest path to broadly capable robots is to work on clearly defined, high impact problems. That's why we're starting where the need is most acute, and the environment is most exacting: the factory floor, in partnership with Rivian.

We are building a lean, collaborative team where every individual has a massive impact. Researchers and engineers work hand in hand with hardware every day. We’re looking for builders who are passionate about robotics and live for the challenge of making systems work in the real world.

Explore opportunities at https://www.mindrobotics.com/

Name: PSYONIC
Description: PSYONIC is an advanced bionics company that is creating fully integrated, super-charged extensions for humans and robotics systems. Fully adaptable and incredibly affordable. Proudly designed and manufactured in San Diego, California.

Name: Contoro Robotics
Description: Contoro Robotics is an Austin-based robotics startup that is revolutionizing industrial automation with AI-powered robots, focused on automating the unloading of floor-loaded trailer and shipping containers from trucks. Their pioneering human-in-the-loop (HITL) model ensures over 99% success in real-world applications, bridging the gap between AI limitations and the commercial viability of advanced robotics solutions.

Name: mundane
Description: founded by Stanford robotics researchers, we're building humanoids that are useful beyond just lab demos, but in actual real-world deployments.

Name: Andromeda
Description:
Hello! Welcome to Andromeda. We’re a robotics company, working to make a positive difference in the world.

We’re building Abi, the world’s first truly empathetic companion robot, who isn’t just designed to assist, but to be your best friend. With a heart full of empathy and a spirit of kindness, Abi creates deep, meaningful connections with people, making the world a little warmer, a little brighter, and a lot more connected. Just like the beloved characters in your favourite stories, Abi is here to listen, understand, and share joyful moments.

Abi, has been co-developed with aged care and assisted living homes to:
 Provide personalised companionship to residents more often
 Interact and connect with residents individually and in groups
 Genuinely relate to each person – speaking their preferred language, and remembering faces, names and conversations
 Meaningfully connect with residents, improving health & wellbeing

 Invite Abi to meet your team 
Visit andromedarobotics.ai for more info and to book a demo with Abi. We’re currently working with aged care and assisted living homes in Australia and the US, and we’d love to bring Abi to meet you and your team.

 Keen to join our team?

Name: Control Barrier Functions
Description: Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) are mathematical tools in robotics and control theory used to guarantee a system stays within safe operating regions, preventing undesired behaviors like collisions by constraining control inputs at each time step, often solved via quadratic programming for real-time safety filtering in dynamic systems. They define a "safe set" and use a function to ensure the system's future states remain in this set (forward invariance), making them ideal for ensuring robots avoid obstacles while still performing tasks.

Name: Origami Robotics
Description:
Industrial automation is essential to the future of manufacturing—and fundamentally broken for everyone who isn’t a Fortune 500 company.

Today’s robotics market is built around rigid, over-engineered systems that assume parts never change, volumes are massive, and time-to-deploy doesn’t matter. Automation is sold as a one-time capital asset, but in practice it is a slow, fragile engineering project that collapses the moment a part, fixture, or workflow changes. For small and mid-sized manufacturers, especially machine shops, this model is economically and operationally unworkable. Robotics is supposed to increase flexibility, but today it enforces rigidity.

Origami Robotics exists to invert this model.

We build modular robotic systems powered by chained agents that produce deterministic automation through high-level abstraction. Instead of writing low-level motion code or re-engineering cells for every new part, users deploy reusable “skills” that reason about tasks such as picking, orienting, cleaning, loading, and unloading. These agents are chained together to create predictable, repeatable behavior, without sacrificing flexibility.

Our hardware is designed to reconfigure in minutes, not weeks. Arms, gantries, vision, and end effectors are self-identifying and automatically integrated into the control system, allowing motion, kinematics, and constraints to be generated on the fly. A new CNC job does not require rebuilding the cell, only selecting a new skill chain and, when needed, a simple fixture or nest.

This approach makes high-mix, low-volume automation not just possible, but incredibly useful.

The constraint is no longer the vessel — it is the intelligence that makes the vessel operationally viable. Autonomy today is fragmented across point solutions, brittle outside controlled conditions, incapable of coordinating at fleet scale, and blind to its own operational data. Quantis AI Labs exists to close that gap.

We do not build vessels. We build the intelligence layer that makes vessels operationally autonomous.

The stack:

Mission Compute — proprietary deterministic mission compute: low-SWaP, modular and stackable from nano-UAV to large USV and AUV.

Perception & Navigation — sensor fusion and navigation intelligence engineered for degraded sensors, dynamic weather, and high-traffic waterways.

Mission Autonomy — mission-level decision software built for meaningful independence from human supervision. Autonomous, not remote-controlled.

Fleet Intelligence — a cloud-based coordination layer for distributed multi-vessel operations, with every mission feeding a continuous learning loop.

The same stack extends beyond the maritime domain — to robotics, advanced manufacturing, and critical infrastructure. The sea is where it is validated first.

One platform family. Every class of unmanned system. Built to learn.

Occurring every two weeks, our Neuroscience-Robotics workshops are designed to be engaging, dynamic, and deeply enriching. Each workshop is anticipated to span 2 hours. Students will be guided throughout this program by industry experts Sahar Jahanikia, founder of Jahanikia NeuroLab, and Dominick Lee, founder of GyroPalm. As part of this program, research students will be provided with hardware materials and components needed to effectively explore the related topics in the course.

Description:
TowBotics is a retrofit, remote-controlled trailer hitching system that empowers RV owners to maneuver, lift, and hitch safely - improving safety and restoring travel independence without physical strain. From over 100 interviews with RV owners, the message was consistent: hitching isn't just frustrating - it’s the reason many stop using their trailers. Owners described it as “the last step before freedom,” but also the most frustrating and riskiest one.

This is where Towbotics comes in. Towbotics replaces the traditional tongue jack with a powered robotic system that lifts and micro-aligns the trailer using a handheld remote. Its precision actuators offer inch-level positioning, while built-in safety features - like stop-on-disconnect and dead-man controls - ensure safe operation even on uneven terrain. The system retrofits directly onto standard tongue-jack mounts, requiring no truck-side changes.

In testing on full-size class 3 trailers, TowBotics enabled first-time users to consistently hitch solo in under three minutes with minimal instruction. By removing physical strain and operational guesswork, it restores confidence and independence to a generation of RVers.

Square Hammer Labs builds failure intelligence and prevention for robots. We classify the root cause from sensor data, pair it with the fix, and turn every incident into a reusable lesson that compounds across your fleet.

Name: Project GLEN
Description:
Project G.L.E.N., formally known as “Enhancing Tornado Research: A Case for Transitioning the Enhanced Fujita Scale,” is an ongoing initiative aimed at advancing tornado research through the development and deployment of an unmanned tornado probe. Through the Gale Level Environmental Navigator (G.L.E.N.) probe, a remote-controlled vehicle equipped with advanced meteorological sensors and innovative design features, we aim to collect real-time, onsite data from within storm systems and tornadoes. This approach allows for direct measurement of internal atmospheric conditions such as wind speeds, pressure fluctuations, temperature, humidity, and other storm dynamics while removing human risk from interception, significantly enhancing the safety of storm research.  Additionally, while current tornado ratings rely heavily on post-storm damage surveys, which may not accurately reflect the full strength or behavior of a tornado, Project G.L.E.N. seeks to provide a more objective basis for tornado classification, bridging the gap between damage-based assessments and recorded metrics. 
     The project’s initial phase focuses on localized data collection to validate sensor performance, refine instrumentation methods, and optimize probe design. Collected data from our final, revised design will be analyzed for statistically significant trends, providing the empirical foundation for potential enhancements or revisions to the Enhanced Fujita (EF) Scale.

Mechanical fixturing, end-of-arm tooling fabrication, PLC integration, and safety engineering are delegated to regional integration partners. We stay in the AI/software lane.

Description:
“The Pivot Flywheel” transforms Starlink-connected mixed-fleet irrigation pivots into a continuously improving agronomic intelligence network.

Rather than replacing existing irrigation pivots, Fieldbot retrofits virtually any mixed-fleet irrigation pivot with a patented intelligence layer that converts legacy equipment into autonomous crop platforms. As each upgraded pivot operates, onboard high-resolution cameras and multispectral sensors capture plant-level imagery observations. Using edge computing and Starlink connectivity, a central AI model analyzes this information in near real time to identify crop stresses, diseases, insects, weeds, nutrient deficiencies, and irrigation needs.

By learning across thousands of upgraded pivots spanning multiple farms, regions, climates, and crops, the system recognizes patterns no individual farm could detect. It returns hyper-localized recommendations, autonomously applying water, fertilizer, and crop protection products with increasing precision. Every application reinforces the AI data flywheel.

A key differentiator are the AI agents that capture farmer knowledge, management decisions, and local practices, transforming unwritten experience into structured intelligence combined with machine vision data.

Universal Fieldbot Precision Upgrades solve the slow operating speeds of conventional irrigation pivots through patented ultra-high-speed constant move operation. Upgraded pivots complete daily 90-minute crop imaging passes followed by 90-minute crop protection passes when needed, enabling problems to be detected and corrected before they spread.

As The Pivot Flywheel expands, every upgraded pivot contributes new proprietary plant-level observations, making the network smarter. Over time, this proprietary dataset compounds into agronomic superintelligence that can autonomously optimize crop management through AI agent licensing for agronomic decisions and machine autonomy for any crop, on any acre, anywhere in the world.

Texas Intelligent Machines (TIM) is building the next generation of large-scale robotic systems designed not just to operate individual machines, but to coordinate and manage entire fleets of robots in real time.

Headquartered in Texas, TIM focuses on a new class of robotics: systems-level intelligence for distributed machines. Our technology enables hundreds or thousands of robots industrial arms, mobile units, drones, and autonomous agents to operate as a unified, adaptive system rather than isolated devices.

At the core of TIM’s approach is a hybrid intelligence architecture that combines centralized orchestration with distributed decision-making at the agent level. This allows robotic systems to remain efficient, resilient, and operational even in dynamic, high-pressure environments or under limited connectivity.
By integrating real-world machines with their digital counterparts in a continuous feedback loop, including proprietary decision frameworks for decentralized coordination, TIM creates synchronized physical–virtual systems capable of simulation-driven optimization, adaptive coordination, and scalable deployment.

Our mission is to redefine how robotic systems are deployed and managed at scale from advanced manufacturing and logistics to autonomous infrastructure and beyond.

In addition to robotics systems, TIM develops its own AI frameworks that power decentralized decision-making and enable scalable coordination across robotic fleets.

We are not just building robots,

Description: At SLA Robotics, our aim to revolutionize access to locations and information in regions that are remote and dangerous to humans and other robots. Name: ASME Letters in Translational Robotics
Description:
PURPOSE
The ASME Letters in Translational Robotics will provide rapid publication of high quality, translational research results, demonstrated with a prototype leading to a minimally viable product. It will also include archival innovations that lead to new best practice in design, realization and deployment of robotic devices and systems. It will bring advances in robotics research to the practicing engineer by emphasizing creative solutions to real-world problems and sharing innovations in implementation details. By considering shorter-form papers, as well as traditional length papers in an accelerated timeframe, this journal will expedite the application and translation of science, engineering and design principles in robotics into new or improved technological products. It will support use-inspired, translational research that will drive future robotic technologies and engineering solutions with societal impact.

SCOPE
Translational research results demonstrated with prototypes leading to a minimally viable product such as: Use-inspired design (function, form, architecture, operation), innovations and associated risks, and the practical implementation; Challenges and solutions for integration of large multidisciplinary projects; Application-driven robot architectures that encompass agents, tasks, and operational environment. Identify challenges, find innovative solutions, and develop performance measurements. Provide examples of such innovation and invention; Innovative designs (components, subsystems, and systems); Validation of innovation and impact on real-world problems; Methods for design, analysis and algorithms leading to real, reliable robots; Innovations in system integration, and use-inspired cyber-physical systems; Case studies of application by a manufacturer or end user; Innovations and practices in robot design for safe implementation of robotic devices and systems; Reduction of robot patents to practice.

Description:

Afterwards, the preparation for the competitions truly began. We spent the first few weeks brainstorming and prototyping ideas for our robot. Despite having limited time to meet, our team successfully completed our robot design while learning a lot and having fun.

Name: Wilder Robotics
Description:
We are field operators. We build for field operators.

Robots are moving onto real properties, real sites, real jobs. The industry doesn’t have the standards, the service network, or the hardware channel ready for them — and the gap will show up first as a claim, an audit, or a courtroom.

Wilder Robotics builds all three:

• Pask — an open specification and open-source verifier for signed robot action records. AGPL-3.0. Reference implementation on GitHub. IETF draft (draft-wilder-scitt-physical-site-engagement-receipt-00) filing July 28, 2026.

• Robotkeepers — a trained field-service network for robot-ready spaces. Deployment, calibration, and recovery. Someone to call when the machine stops making sense.

• Robots — a deliberately-small catalog of the physical machines we deploy on our own properties. Yarbo for grounds. Beatbot for water.

Physical AI will need standards, service networks, and serviced hardware before it needs more robots. We build all three. We call them the boring parts.

Standards work happens in the open. The specification is public first because it has to be — the rest gets published as it hardens on our own properties.

Wilder Robotics is the technology arm of Wilder Management Inc., a privately held real-estate operating company. The balance sheet runs on operating cash flow from the property business, which means Wilder Robotics is not venture-funded and does not have to be. Our technology is built to serve field operations first and become commercially available second — on the timeline the work actually requires, not on a fundraising clock.

Built by Rob Wilder, a career property operator.

Name: Taloshub.io
Description:
TalosHub captures real manufacturing workflows and turns them into structured training data for robotics companies, VLA model builders, robot OEMs, and industrial AI teams.

Robots that work in factories need more than lab demonstrations. They need data from real production environments: machine states, fixture variance, operator workarounds, exceptions, recoveries, and workflow context.

TalosHub builds manufacturing-native task packs from active facilities. Each pack can include multi-view video, machine-state-aligned metadata, phase segmentation, exception and recovery annotations, schema documentation, sample loaders, train/validation/test splits, and white-labeled handoff artifacts.

We are not a raw footage vendor. We deliver scoped, documented, QA-gated task packs that robotics teams can inspect, load, and train against.

If you are building robots for manufacturing, TalosHub helps you close the factory data gap without spending months building capture operations in-house.

Hands-on build nights and teleoperation sessions

Name: Nexterity, Inc.
Description:
OUR PRODUCT

Nexterity has developed a hands-free robotic tool for the (un)bolting of industrial pipeline infrastructure. (Un)bolting of pipelines is very common and required for routine maintenance and construction of all piping infrastructure. Today, this is primarily accomplished with hand tools/wrenches or electrically powered impact wrenches. These tools require a human user to be in close proximity to a pipe and its bolted joint.

SAFETY

(Un)bolting interface activities are safely managed by a human-in-the-loop via remote control. With our hands-free tool, humans and their hands are able to distance themselves from the pipe and its joint for safety. This distance not only allows for additional safety in the bolting process but also clears enough space to allow a nimble robotic tool to better position itself in front of the pipe joint. With this additional clearance, the robotic tool can interface with multiple bolts at a time.

SPEED

This dexterity and access enables the tool to provide a speed advantage of up to 8x in the (un)bolting process versus the current manual alternative. 

QUALITY

When interfacing with multiple bolts at a time via machine, there is significant reduction of human error in the bolting process. This allows our technology to deliver equal if not better quality than human labor, without requiring the physical exertion. Our tool allows for torque setting within +/- 10 ft*lbs of a target torque and provides the consistency and reliability of a programmed machine.

Shipwreck City is an ongoing effort to document, photograph, and share the sunken vessels and debris resting on the floor of Lake Union — one of Seattle's most beloved waterways.

This lake has been part of the homelands of the Duwamish Tribe for thousands of years, who used these waters for travel, fishing, and daily life long before the city was built.

In the late 1800s, after the arrival of Euro-American settlers, Lake Union became a working waterway for industry, travel, and recreation. Its bottom holds a remarkable record of the past: a hidden landscape shaped over time as vessels and debris collect on the lakebed.

Many of these submerged sites are unknown to the people who swim, paddle, sail, and fly above them each day. Shipwreck City brings this hidden world into view. By creating a visual archive of each site, the project shows how the lake continues to evolve. It invites us to think about preservation, pollution, and our shared responsibility to care for urban waterways.

Through photography, video, and research, we aim to make these underwater stories accessible while encouraging deeper connection to Lake Union and its connected waterways.

EconomicOS, real-time micropayments, autonomous contract execution, and per-robot financial identity at machine speed.

Fihan Edge gives autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) and industrial automated systems the judgment to

  off: move slowly to avoid collisions, or risk safety to maintain throughput.

  deterministic, un-overridable safety supervisor: The Fihan Safe House.
    
    ---
    
    HOW FIHAN EDGE WORKS (THE 3-LAYER LOOP):
    
     1. SEE (Instant Onboard Perception)
    Processes 3D LiDAR and vision point clouds locally on edge hardware. No raw data is sent to the
  cloud, giving robots real-time situational awareness with zero network latency.
    
     2. DECIDE (Rehearsed AI Intelligence)
    Driven by deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policies trained across thousands of edge-case
  scenarios in high-fidelity simulators. The robot plans smooth, efficient paths and eases off speed
  in uncertain environments.
    
     3. STAY SAFE (Deterministic Safety Supervision)
    An independent, zero-exception safety filter sits directly between the neural network decision and
  the physical motor actuators. If a proposed move breaches safety envelopes, the safety layer
  overrides or slows the robot instantly.
    
    ---
    
    ENGINEERING & COMPLIANCE HIGHLIGHTS:
    • Built Natively in Rust: Zero garbage-collection pauses for predictable, real-time control.
    • Ultra-Low Latency: < 2ms point-cloud preprocessing, < 10ms p99 end-to-end perception, and < 0.
  1ms safety checks per tick.
    • Low Power & On-Device: Sustained power consumption under 15W on NVIDIA Jetson Orin compute nodes.
    • Standards Alignment: Designed toward IEC 61508 SIL-2, ISO 3691-4, and DO-178C safety standards.
    • Seamless Integration: Deployable as a native Rust SDK, C library, or ROS 2 (Humble)
