Name: REFL3X
Description:
REFL3X is building reflex architecture for real-world robotics.
Today’s AI systems — including LLMs and other high-level planning models — are powerful, but intelligence alone is not enough. In the physical world, systems fail at the boundary between software and reality: contact, friction, slip, overload, collision, and sensor degradation.

Biology solved this long ago. Humans do not rely on reasoning alone to move safely — we rely on nerves, reflexes, and a spinal control layer that reacts before higher cognition can catch up. REFL3X applies that same principle to robotics.

We design deterministic, physically grounded control architectures that sit between intelligence and actuation, ensuring autonomous systems remain stable, safe, and reliable even when planners are wrong, delayed, or operating under uncertainty.

Reflex before reason. Stability before scale.

Name: dexset
Description:
Robots do not learn from clean theory. They learn from messy reality.

dexset is the real-world data layer for robotics and physical AI. We help teams that build humanoids, warehouse robots, industrial automation, and autonomous systems collect, annotate, structure, validate, and deliver the training data their models actually need — captured from the environments where those machines will work.

What we do:
• Real-world video collection across commercial, industrial, warehouse, residential, and controlled environments
• Egocentric and exocentric capture — head-mounted, wrist-mounted, and calibrated multi-camera rigs, frame-synced
• Human task demonstrations designed around your model's requirements, with controlled variation and outcome labels
• Robotics-specific annotation: bounding boxes, segmentation masks, 21-point hand pose, task states, and failure events
• Teleoperation data loops that turn every operator intervention into a training signal
• Deliberate failure-case capture — occlusions, mis-grips, slips, clutter — the scenarios that break deployment
• ML-ready delivery in COCO, YOLO, Pascal VOC, JSON, CSV, or your custom schema, versioned and validated

Every dataset ships with consent records, capture provenance, and quality scores. Our workflows are designed to align with GDPR, UK GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, PIPL, APPI, and LGPD, and our operators and annotators are fairly paid — quality data should never come from exploitative labor.

Simulation has value. But deployment needs variation, friction, and unpredictable human behavior. We capture the data robots need to improve: real tasks, real environments, real interactions, real failures.

Name: Mecha Robotics Corporation
Description:
Mecha Robotics Corporation builds robotic systems that amplify human capability in the most demanding environments. Our mission is simple: to 11-foot-tall to 30-foot-tall mecha robotic designed machines that work with people, not instead of them—creating safer, faster, and more precise operations across industries where human strength, endurance, and access face natural limits. Gaming, mobility, commercial, industrial, scientific, policing/crowd control, military, emergency management, disaster relief and more.

Our exoskeletons and mecha armor reduce injury risk in logistics, construction, and emergency response; Piloted, autonomous, and a combination piloted/autonomous configurations that extend reach for gaming, inspection, material handling, crowd control, combat and remote operations. Our autonomous and piloted configurations that combine perception, adaptive control, and intuitive interfaces to enable seamless human-robot collaboration.

Our differentiator is pragmatic engineering focused on deployment. Every unit is modular, maintainable, and built for serviceability in the field. By prioritizing safety, reliability, and operator acceptance, we ensure that our systems generate measurable outcomes: outdoor gaming, higher visibility of workers normally on foot, mobility alternative for those with walking/standing disabilities, higher throughput, safer work zones, and workers shielded for hazardous, remote, or precision-critical environments.

We work with global partners in logistics, energy, aerospace, mobility and public safety to deliver solutions that solve operational challenges where automation alone is insufficient. Our approach blends mechanical engineering, autonomous research, and human-centered design into systems that extend—not replace—human capability.

Follow Mecha Robotics for updates on technology breakthroughs, deployments, partnerships, and opportunities to collaborate as we build a future where humans and machines operate as true teammates.

Name: Robot Revival LLC
Description:
Robot Revival is a specialized repair and support business focused on keeping legacy inspection robots—especially the SuperDroid GPK‐32 platform—working in the field for as long as possible. We help home inspectors, pest control operators, insurance adjusters, contractors, and facility teams avoid costly downtime by diagnosing, repairing, and refurbishing the robots they depend on to see into crawlspaces, ceilings, and hard‐to‐reach spaces.

Our services cover GPK‐32 platform repair, electrical and power troubleshooting, drivetrain and track/wheel issues, camera and lighting systems, and preventive maintenance for older mobile inspection robots. Instead of pushing expensive replacements, we focus on extending the life of proven equipment with practical, field-tested fixes and clear communication on cost and turnaround.

Based in North Carolina and serving customers across the U.S., Robot Revival combines hands-on robotics repair experience with an understanding of real-world inspection work, tight schedules, and regulatory documentation needs. If your inspection robot is aging, out‐of‐warranty, or no longer supported by the original manufacturer, we help bring it back to productive service so you can keep inspecting, documenting, and delivering for your own clients.

Description:

SPADE brings together students from diverse STEM backgrounds who share a passion for aerospace systems, intelligent technologies, and creative engineering design.
The organization focuses on practical learning through prototype development, design challenges, workshops, and inter-disciplinary projects that mirror real-world engineering environments. From propulsion concepts and flight computers to AI-assisted design tools and rapid prototyping, SPADE encourages members to move beyond theory and actively build, test, and iterate.
Beyond technical work, SPADE aims to cultivate leadership, teamwork, and professional growth by organizing campus events, industry talks, and collaborative initiatives with other student groups. Its mission is to empower community-college students to gain meaningful engineering experience early in their academic journey and prepare them for competitive transfers, research opportunities, and future careers in aerospace, robotics, and advanced technology fields.
